transcript:
Header: 
Date: 2026-08-05 15:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lucas Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Redwood CSM); David Kim (Parcelly Labs CTO), Aisha Nadeem (Lead ML Eng), Tom Ruiz (SRE), Helen Park (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick hosted API demo showing streaming behavior, tips for parameters (temperature, max_tokens, top_p), and robust retry/backoff patterns including idempotency tokens. Console tour briefly showed per-route metrics and Optimize suggestions.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Lucas Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Lucas, i'm an AE at Redwood. quick agenda, we'll do a short hosted gen demo, show streaming, parameters and then retry/playbook, and end with next steps. sound good?
[00:08] David Kim: yep that works for us, thanks. we mostly want to see low-latency behavior for mobile chat and how to handle intermittent spikes.
[00:15] Priya Sharma: great, i'll drive the demo. real quick — are you currently using any model provider or self-host today?
[00:20] Aisha Nadeem: we're using a mix, small stuff on CloudEndpt endpoints, and an internal fine-tuned model for summaries. but it's a bit slow and costs are spiky.
[00:30] Priya Sharma: got it, thanks. i'll share my screen — showing the hosted chat endpoint request. this is a basic streaming call using server-sent events (SSE) in our client.
[00:40] [screen noise]
[00:45] Priya Sharma: so you can see the request body — messages array, model: rdx-large-1, temperature: 0.2, max_tokens: 256, stream: true. we prefer lower temperature for deterministic chat.
[00:58] Tom Ruiz: quick q — when you stream, how often do tokens arrive? is it by token or by chunk?
[01:05] Priya Sharma: good q. streaming depends on the runtime and model; typically we emit chunks ~ every 200-800ms for conversational prompts at normal token rates. smaller chunks can increase overhead so we batch tokens into SSE frames. it's not per-token network packet usually.
[01:20] Aisha Nadeem: and what about chunk_size or chunk_delay? are those knobs we control?
[01:25] Priya Sharma: we expose a couple of things — the API has a response_chunk_size preference and we support streaming params in SDKs to tune flushing. also our runtime has continuous batching so client-side chunk tuning should be conservative.
[01:36] Lucas Chen: i'll pause here to show the console metrics for that route — latency p50/p95, tokens per sec, and a streaming breakdown.
[01:45] [console click sounds]
[01:48] Priya Sharma: on the console you'll see per-route cost and token breakdown. Optimize will suggest batching sizes and a quantization profile if you want to lower cost on sustained traffic.
[02:02] Helen Park: can you explain quantization profile? our ML lead asked about fp16 vs int8.
[02:08] Priya Sharma: sure — Optimize recommends a model variant and quantization setting depending on latency and quality tradeoffs. for example, rdx-large-1-int8 will be cheaper but might shift a few edge-case tokens, we show QA evals in the console.
[02:22] David Kim: going back to retries — our mobile clients see flaky networks. what's best practice for retrying streaming calls?
[02:28] Priya Sharma: streaming retries are tricky. we recommend using small idempotency tokens per user-turn and switching to a non-streaming resume endpoint on reconnect. pattern: client sends idempotency token, if connection drops, client checks server-side partial output via status endpoints and resumes with remaining instructions.
[02:44] Tom Ruiz: is there a resume token or KV cache we can rely on?
[02:48] Priya Sharma: Redwood's runtime maintains a KV cache for short-lived sessions (we call it kv cache, sometimes transcribed as KV cash, haha). the resume workflow uses the idempotency key to fetch cached KV plus request context. it's subject to TTL — default 10 minutes for hosted, configurable for Dedicated.
[03:04] Aisha Nadeem: TTLs are important. we can't keep PII in cache beyond compliance windows.
[03:10] Marta Lopez: good flag — we'll add notes in the security pack about KV cache retention and customer-configurable TTLs for Private/Dedicated.
[03:18] [brief cross talk]
[03:22] Priya Sharma: for retry strategies: one, client-side exponential backoff with jitter. two, use idempotency tokens for resume/dedup. three, detect partial streams; if you see the stream cut at a token boundary, try a resume with last confirmed token. four, server-side fallbacks: route to cheaper model variant if the primary is overloaded.
[03:45] David Kim: how do you detect token boundaries reliably? transcripts sometimes cut mid-word.
[03:50] Priya Sharma: yep, imperfect. we mark chunk boundaries with sequence numbers in SSE metadata so client can dedupe or request the next sequence. small network packet losses can cause repeated tokens but idempotency + sequence numbers help.
[04:05] Helen Park: can Redwood enforce concurrency limits per API key to protect us from runaway mobile clients?
[04:12] Lucas Chen: yes, we have per-key concurrency and rate limits — configurable via the Console. you can set rate limits per route and set burst windows; we also provide token-level billing to see cost per user.
[04:25] [pause, typing]
[04:30] Priya Sharma: i'll switch to a quick simulated demo. calling the hosted chat endpoint now with 5 concurrent mobile clients to show streaming and one client disconnect mid-stream.
[04:40] [simulated demo audio]
[04:43] Priya Sharma: ok i just dropped client 3 — you'll see the server record a partial session and a resume key in the logs. now i'll reattach using the idempotency token and resume=true.
[04:55] Tom Ruiz: i see a small delay on resume, is that due to KV retrieval?
[04:59] Priya Sharma: yes, there's a KV lookup and sometimes a cold fetch if the KV was pushed to slower storage. on Dedicated we can pin KV to faster storage and reduce resume latency.
[05:12] Lucas Chen: cost note — resuming may re-generate a small overlap; we bill for tokens produced. Optimize can recommend caching prefixes to avoid re-sending long context that is repeated across turns.
[05:28] Aisha Nadeem: what's the recommendation for max_tokens for mobile short answers? we want 1-2 sentence replies.
[05:35] Priya Sharma: set max_tokens low (40-80) and lower temperature. also use stop sequences. you can use token_budget heuristics on Console for per-session spend caps.
[05:48] David Kim: what about early stopping — can the model stream a partial answer and we patch in a follow-up?
[05:54] Priya Sharma: common pattern: optimistic streaming with early stop on confidence heuristics. Redwood doesn't expose model internals like token confidence but you can implement a heuristic on length and punctuation, or run a small follow-up scoring request.
[06:08] Helen Park: security path — we will need SOC 2 docs and network connectivity doc. will Redwood provide guidance on VPC peering and private CP?
[06:15] Marta Lopez: yes, i'll send the security pack (SOC2 report, encryption-at-rest notes, KMS integration guide) and our VPC private control-plane architecture doc. for on-prem or air-gapped we have a Private package.
[06:28] David Kim: good. pricing — are there cost tools to estimate per-chat session?
[06:33] Lucas Chen: console does per-route cost projections using token distributions; during onboarding we can run a simulated traffic profile so you get an estimate. i'll add a sandbox with credits so you can run 1000 short sessions.
[06:46] [pause]
[06:50] Priya Sharma: switching gears — idempotency token format: we recommend userID-turnID and server validates uniqueness for 24 hours; you can roll your own. also suggest keeping seat limits for concurrency per user.
[07:04] Tom Ruiz: how do we instrument retries so we don't double-charge users?
[07:09] Priya Sharma: Redwood treats requests with same idempotency token as a single logical request for billing dedupe window (configurable). we still bill produced tokens, but dedupe prevents double-invoke billing when a retry triggers duplicate generation.
[07:24] Aisha Nadeem: what backoff schedule is best? linear, exp, truncated exp?
[07:28] Priya Sharma: truncated exponential with jitter is standard — base 200ms, cap 8s, random jitter to avoid thundering herd. for streaming reconnects, quick retries for first 2 attempts then longer windows.
[07:45] David Kim: any sample client code? we can integrate ours in React Native.
[07:49] Priya Sharma: yes, we'll share SDK snippets for JS mobile and Retrofit for Android. the SDK handles SSE frame parsing and sequence dedupe.
[07:58] [screen: console - Optimize tab]
[08:02] Priya Sharma: here Optimize suggests a batching window for your workload based on doc size distribution — it estimates 18% cost savings with a 40ms batching window and prefix caching for repeated greetings.
[08:18] Helen Park: 18% is significant. are there quality regressions?
[08:22] Priya Sharma: for our eval set we saw negligible regression; console provides A/B eval comparisons, and you can pin rollout percentages.
[08:33] Tom Ruiz: how about fallback policies? if rdx-large-1 is overloaded do you fall back automatically?
[08:39] Priya Sharma: yes — smart routing allows policy: prefer primary, fallback to quantized variant or smaller model. you can set fallback thresholds in the route config. critical calls can opt for no-fallback.
[08:51] David Kim: can we get alerts if fallback starts happening often?
[08:55] Lucas Chen: yes, Console alerts and tracing show fallback frequency with root-cause traces.
[09:02] [brief pause]
[09:06] Priya Sharma: time permitting, i'll demonstrate a short load test: firing 200 concurrent short chats to mimic peak hour. watch the latency p95.
[09:15] [load test noise]
[09:19] Priya Sharma: p50 stays low, p95 climbs — Optimize would recommend raising reserved concurrency or switching to a dedicated pool for predictable throughput.
[09:30] Aisha Nadeem: what are commit terms for Dedicated? monthly or annually?
[09:34] Lucas Chen: Dedicated has monthly and annual commitments, we usually recommend annual for cost predictability but can start with monthly burst to Dedicated for initial tests.
[09:44] Helen Park: one more on compliance — if we need EU data residency, are regions available?
[09:49] Marta Lopez: yes, hosted regions include EU; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in EU or Private with on-prem. we'll include region options in the security pack.
[09:59] David Kim: ok let's recap next steps before we run out of time.
[10:03] Lucas Chen: recap — Lucas enable sandbox credits and send pricing; Priya send sample SDK code + load test config; Marta send security pack and network guide; Aisha to share PII classification. schedule deep-dive next week.
[10:15] Aisha Nadeem: thanks, that works. couple of follow-ups — can we get a sample idempotency implementation and an example resume flow?
[10:21] Priya Sharma: yes, i'll include that in the follow-up email with code snippets and diagrams.
[10:28] David Kim: perfect. thanks everyone.
[10:31] Lucas Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and next steps.
[10:36] [meeting end]

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (KV cache heard as KV cash), some product names abbreviated (rdx-large may show as rdx lrg), minor speaker attribution glitches. Full logs and console screenshots will be attached in the follow-up email.
